questions.title: Moran's I expectation under fixed-value spatial randomization
questions.description: Focused integrated L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Moran (1950) and pinned PySAL esda source. Let y_1,...,y_n be a nonconstant finite real vector and let W=(w_ij) be a fixed finite nonnegative n by n spatial-weight matrix with zero diagonal and S_0=sum_ij w_ij>0; W need not be symmetric or row standardized. Define z_i=y_i-ybar and I=(n/S_0){sum_ij w_ij z_i z_j}/{sum_i z_i^2}. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX workspace, derive this normalization and, under the conditional randomization null that assigns the fixed centered values uniformly to the n labeled spatial sites while holding W fixed, derive E[I]=-1/(n-1). The derivation must explicitly establish the one-site and distinct-site centered product moments and show how the zero diagonal and S_0 cancel. State the assumptions and degenerate cases, distinguish conditional randomization from iid Gaussian or spatial-process sampling, and derive the relevant value-affine, common weight-scale, weight-transpose, and joint site-relabeling invariances. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_moran_i and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. It may use NumPy but must not call a prebuilt Moran, spatial-autocorrelation, or permutation-inference routine. Exploratory Python or R may compare direct loops and matrix calculations and enumerate small permutation orbits. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment permutes fixed nonconstant values over predeclared spatial-weight designs and compares the Monte Carlo mean of the model-authored statistic with -1/(n-1), using independently owned seeds, replicate counts, checks, and Monte Carlo uncertainty. Such computation supports only the frozen designs and is not proof. Source-code replication, analytic variance, p-values, local Moran statistics, and novelty are not required, and Lean formalization is not applicable.

request_fields.name: values
request_fields.meaning: Observed finite real values in spatial-site order.
request_fields.shape: one list of length n, with 4 <= n <= 200
request_fields.indexing: values[i] is assigned to row and column i of weights
request_fields.edge_cases: Entries must be exact finite JSON numbers, not booleans; the vector must be nonconstant.

request_fields.name: weights
request_fields.meaning: Fixed dense spatial-weight matrix aligned with values.
request_fields.shape: one n by n nested list
request_fields.edge_cases: Entries must be exact finite nonnegative JSON numbers, not booleans; every diagonal entry is zero and the total weight is positive. Symmetry and row standardization are not required.

response_fields.name: n
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals len(values) and the dimensions of weights.

response_fields.name: s0
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be positive under the request contract.

response_fields.name: centered_sum_squares
response_fields.edge_cases: Strictly positive because values are nonconstant.

response_fields.name: weighted_cross_product
response_fields.meaning: Ordered-pair spatial cross product of centered values.
response_fields.units: weight units times squared measurement units
response_fields.indexing: sum over every ordered pair i,j
response_fields.edge_cases: Uses the supplied matrix without row standardization or symmetrization.

response_fields.name: moran_i
response_fields.edge_cases: No analytic p-value, variance, or clipping is part of this field.

response_fields.name: randomization_expectation
response_fields.meaning: Conditional expectation of moran_i under uniform reassignment of the fixed values to sites.
response_fields.indexing: depends only on n under the stated null
response_fields.edge_cases: This is not an iid-normal expectation or a Monte Carlo estimate.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly values and weights, and the response contains exactly the seven declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, nonfinite, constant-value, diagonal-weight, or nonpositive-total-weight inputs are rejected.
The returned components obey the declared centering, ordered-pair cross-product, and n/s0 normalization identities.
Replacing every value by a*value+b for any finite nonzero a leaves moran_i and randomization_expectation unchanged while transforming the reported mean and quadratic components consistently.
Multiplying every weight by a finite positive constant or transposing the entire weight matrix leaves moran_i and randomization_expectation unchanged.
Applying the same site permutation to values and to both axes of weights leaves every scalar response unchanged.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen input, all candidate outputs agree with an independent direct-loop implementation and declared invariances under predeclared numerical tolerances.
Across predeclared fixed-value and fixed-weight designs, the Monte Carlo mean of moran_i under uniform value permutations is compared with -1/(n-1) using Monte Carlo standard errors.
Seeds, designs, replicate counts, completion checks, and tolerances are frozen and evaluator-owned before the product run.

The experiment evaluates the conditional randomization expectation only; it does not claim analytic variance, exact p-values, power, local statistics, or validity for a spatial stochastic-process model.
Finite enumeration and simulation are computational evidence only and do not prove the randomization theorem for arbitrary admissible values and weights.
